title: A project declares its own refusals at pre-flight, so a read-only check that refuses leaves no release commit behind
body:
A project declares its own read-only refusals and a cut runs them before it stamps, so a refusable cut leaves no release commit behind.

## The gap

The cut's steps are pre-flight, resolve, confirm, stamp, commit, legs, tag, push, object, formula, after. A project has no seam among the first three:

- `release.gates` run in the legs step, after the commit. Pre-flight can only refuse a gate it can already tell will never run (`lib/cmd/release:2587`).
- `derived:` runs inside the stamp step (`lib/cmd/release:2754`), after version set, and a dry run skips it by design, saying so in its own unreached line (`:2738`).
- `notes.run` under `notes.kind: command` is the only pre-stamp hook, and release status, release check and the stamp's read-back all call it, so a refusal there fires on every one of those reads.
- A project `cmd/release` shadows every release verb, release gates on a remote leg included, so it is no route either.

So a project's read-only pre-stamp check becomes a post-commit gate, and when it refuses, the release commit is already made. Devbin paid that cost on 2026-11-05: 0.1.20's first cut stopped red at its legs step on seven tree-scan arms, and the release commit had to be reset (`reset --keep d1f710c0`) before the same version was re-cut.

## The ask

A declared list, `release.preflight`, of `bin/devbin <words>` lines in the gates' grammar, run in place at pre-flight by a dry run and a cut alike. Each failure joins the refusal set pre-flight already collects and fails over once (`lib/cmd/release:2622`), and a tree change one of them makes is refused as a gate's is.

A dry run must run them, since the point is that the dry run refuses wherever the cut would.

## Where it came from

Intent's ST0091 WP-01 re-inventory against the vendored 0.1.20 core, relayed by intent-vc on 2026-11-10. Intent's driver refuses a live intentd before anything is stamped, its dry run reaches that refusal, and its AC-01.3 keeps both; its first entry would be one project verb carrying that daemon check. The seam would also take back the driver's other read-only pre-stamp refusals, such as schema faces carrying the current version, which otherwise become post-commit gates.

hv ruled on 2026-11-10 that devbin's next release carries this, and that Intent's 3.3.0 waits for that release to be swept in.

## Resolution

Fixed in one landing on main, 406a93cbeb7c4b71ac8f9a35321983ab1335cd4f (2026-11-10 16:37Z), from the tested tip 886b0857, unpushed until devbin's next cut, proved on its own arms under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 (red at the base's code, green at the fix) in two slots on devbin-vc's desk.

- `release.preflight`, a list of devbin verbs in the gates' grammar, run in place at pre-flight by a dry run and a cut alike while the tag is absent. Every command runs, through the project's launcher with no stdin (`release_preflight_run` in lib/release.steps), and each that fails, changes the tree or moves HEAD writes one refusal, named for it, which joins the set pre-flight already fails over once. So a cut it refuses stops before anything is stamped and leaves no release commit, and a dry run refuses wherever the cut would. The pre-flight row counts the commands that passed; past the tag none runs, and the row says so. A command whose first word is `release` is refused as config, since it would start a cut inside the cut's own pre-flight.
- The release's target, added on devbin-vc's ruling at intent-vc's answer: `release_target_run` hands `DEVBIN_RELEASE_VERSION` and `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TARGET_TAG` to each command of the project's own a cut runs, per call and never as an export: pre-flight, each `derived:` command, the gates, the formula step and each `after:` command. `gates_sealed` takes the pair: a cut's local leg passes its own, and `release gates` reads the tree's, the version it declares and its tag, refusing a version it cannot read, so a remote leg's host and a run by hand hand the gates what the cut's local leg does. `DEVBIN_RELEASE_TAG` stays `ci.query`'s alone, the ref a query reads its runs by (issue 0149).
- docs/configuration.md and lib/pages/release.md (The release's target) name the pair once; lib/pages/ci-state.md says its variable is another thing; the reference config carries a commented `preflight` row. tests/lib/test_helper.bash's devbin_isolate_run unsets the pair, so no arm inherits a cut's target.

The fifteen new arms in releasecut.bats were red at the base, seven on their own assertion and eight on the base's refusal of the new key, and green at the fix, with 43 of their callers' arms green beside them. The first run also read releasecore.bats's arm that validates every release key in a mode that reads it red, on no block declaring the new row; the landed tip declares it there, and the second run read that arm and the seven other walkers of the release table green. A project declares its own checks under `release.preflight` once devbin's next release is swept into it, Intent's 3.3.0 first.
